question.prompt: Given the set of \(n\) numbers, \(n\gt1,\) of which one is \(1-\dfrac1n\) and all the others are \(1.\) The arithmetic mean of the \(n\) numbers is:

solutions.explanation:
There are \(n-1\) entries equal to \(1\), together with the single entry \(1-\frac1n\). Their sum is therefore
\[
(n-1)+\left(1-\frac1n\right)=n-\frac1n.
\]
The arithmetic mean is the sum divided by the number of entries. Since \(n\) is an integer greater than \(1\), division by \(n\) is valid, and the mean is
\[
\frac{n-\frac1n}{n}
=1-\frac1{n^2}.
\]
Thus the answer is \(\boxed{1-\frac1{n^2}}\), choice \(\text{D}\).
solutions.title: Divide the total by the number of entries
